pillar_reactions.evidence: The rep deliberately withheld the programme pending a commitment: 'I want to make sure it's something you want to do before I even tell you about it.' No pillar was ever delivered.
Never delivered, and diet was never discussed at any point on the call.

Never delivered as a pillar, though the prospect articulated the need for it himself — 'you need the nagging wife to get you to actually do the dishes. Otherwise, you're just going to stay in the sink' — and the rep answered with a joke rather than a mechanism: 'I can be a nagging wife if you want me to, Taylor.'

anchors.raw: I'm kind of like, I feel like I'm fairly stubborn and I do everything by myself on my own. So I feel like I have the ability to tackle this in my own way.
anchors.note: The competing product is himself. He had already bought two kettlebells and started three movements before the call, which is exactly the free substitute the programme must beat. The rep conceded the capability and argued only that it is harder — an argument about effort, not about outcome.

anchors.raw: I've gone to a lady that stretches me out and everything
anchors.note: An existing paid hands-on practitioner already occupying the back-pain job, and the reason he frames the problem as stretching rather than as strength. Never priced, never contrasted.

anchors.raw: the coaching for six months is, I don't know what it would be in Canadian, but it's six grand US. So that's probably like what, eight, eight grand Canadian.
anchors.note: The number that landed in a Canadian prospect's head was eight thousand, and it was then repeated twice in that form ('The results are worth eight grand', 'you're going to waste eight grand'). Correct as FX, but the effective anchor is 33% above the list price and there is no CAD pricing to reference.

anchors.raw: I feel like it's more of like a commitment when you, you know, join something or get in rather than like just a...
anchors.note: The prospect volunteered the strongest buying belief on the call — that paying is what makes him follow through — and it was met with agreement rather than used. This is the anchor that would have carried the close if the commitment gate had gone the other way.

unmet_demand.want: One fixed sequence he can get up and do, instead of choosing between endless exercises or following a screen
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Almost certainly the core of what the programme delivers, and it was never said. 'when I do follow something online, it's like I'm looking at the screen trying to do stuff, and it's like, I'd rather just have a sequence that works for me, then get up and just do that sequence' is a description of the product, delivered to a rep who had already decided not to present it.

unmet_demand.want: Repair for a year-old lower-back problem — 'I think there's other ways to repair my body'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Positioned as a commitment problem rather than a solvable physical one. The offer was never connected to the back at all, and the prospect's own framing of the programme as one of several possible repair routes went unchallenged.

unmet_demand.want: Something that works without requiring him to become a disciplined person first — 'I want it to be easy and just kind of roll in'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep answered honestly that it will be hard either way. That is true and creditable, but it means the offer as sold requires the prospect to solve the motivation problem himself before buying the thing that solves the motivation problem.
